hints: The common beginning can never be longer than the shortest word. What happens if you line the words up and read them column by column?

Do a vertical scan (or, equivalently, walk a trie built from the words while each node has exactly one child and no word ends there). Check position i in every word; stop at the first column where some word is too short or has a different letter.

1. Take first = words[0].
  2. For i from 0 to first.length − 1: let c = first[i].
  3. For every other word w: if i == w.length or w[i] != c, return first[0..i).
  4. If the loop finishes, the whole first word is shared: return it.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every prefix of the first word from longest to shortest and check whether all words start with it.

approaches.name: Trie
approaches.idea: Insert all words into a trie and walk from the root while there is a single child and no word ends; the walked path is the answer.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Vertical scan: compare column i across all words and stop at the first mismatch. Same time as the trie but no extra memory.

explain: Sample ["planet","plank","plain"]: column 0 is p in all three, column 1 is l, column 2 is a. In column 3 we see n, n and i, a mismatch, so we return the first 3 letters, pla. The invariant is that every column before i matched in all words. Edge cases: an empty word anywhere makes the answer empty right away (the length check), and a single word is its own answer.
recognize: 'Longest beginning that all strings share' → compare characters column by column (or walk a trie of the words).
